The Process

Six stages. One team, the whole way through.

01

Consultation

Free, no obligation. We walk through your goals, take measurements, and review existing conditions.

02

Proposal & Scope

A preliminary proposal, a detailed scope document, and a fixed-price structure broken down by line item.

03

Select Your Materials

Sign in to our material library, browse the full catalogue room by room, and build your palette from home, comparing finishes side by side. Finalize everything in person at the design centre, all in one visit.

04

Drawings & Permits

Our in-house architects create your custom blueprints. We manage the entire City of Toronto permit process.

05

Build & Inspections

Thorough inspections at every milestone to ensure full compliance with the Ontario Building Code.

06

Handover & Warranty

A final walkthrough, backed by our 7-Year Structural Guarantee.

Questions

Everything you'd ask before committing.

What does it cost to build or renovate a home in Toronto?

Cost depends on lot conditions, square footage, finish level and scope. We visit your property first, then build a fixed-price proposal around what we actually find, walked through with you in person at the design centre, not emailed the same week.

How is your fixed-price model different from the cost-plus model most Toronto builders use?

Most high-end builders work on a cost-plus basis, where you pay the actual cost of labour and materials plus a fee on top. The financial risk is yours. Grand Design Build prices the full defined scope before we break ground, so if a cost shifts during construction, that's our risk to manage, not yours.

How long does it take to build a house in the GTA?

A straightforward new build typically runs six to twelve months once permits are approved; a fully custom home tends to run twelve to eighteen months, largely due to design and permitting time.

Do I need to visit multiple showrooms to pick materials?

No. You browse and shortlist materials online through our material library, then finalize every finish, fixture, and material in one visit to our design centre.

Do you handle laneway or garden suites from start to finish?

Yes. We handle the structural, utility and permit requirements specific to Toronto's laneway and garden suite bylaws, from initial design through to final construction.

Are you licensed, and what protection does that give me?

Licensed by the HCRA and fully insured across every project, backed by our own seven-year structural guarantee.

Which neighbourhoods and areas do you build in?

A strong concentration in North York, Forest Hill, Rosedale, Bloor West Village, Leaside, The Beaches, and the surrounding central Toronto neighbourhoods, along with wider GTA municipalities.
